claims.claim: floating leaves of watershield (Brasenia schreberi) live 25–28 days on average
claims.location: p. 281 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 283 (PDF p. 3); p. 285 (PDF p. 5), Table 2
claims.quote: relatively constant around the values of 25-28 d
claims.conditions: annual mean leaf life span 25.5, 28.3 and c. 24.8 d in 1986, 1987 and 1988 (Table 2); leaves individually marked at about weekly intervals in one 50 × 50 cm permanent quadrat in a dense pure stand; Engi-ike, a small shallow irrigation pond in Matsue, Shimane Prefecture, Japan; vegetation periods 154–177 d
claims.note: The abstract's '25–28 d' rounds the three annual means; strictly the range is 24.8–28.3 d. Life span rose through the season to a September peak (Fig. 2), so the annual mean hides a spring–autumn range.

claims.location: p. 281 (PDF p. 1), abstract; p. 285 (PDF p. 5), Table 2 (maximum leaf mass 80.5, 72.6, 52.5 g dry weight m⁻² in 1986–88, read on the page image)
claims.quote: 0.90-1.36, 52.5-80.5g dry weight m-2 and 154.9-243.5 g dry weight
claims.conditions: seasonal maximum mass of floating leaf blades only (no petioles, stems, rhizomes or roots), late August–early September; estimated from leaf length × width regressions (n = 233 leaves, Table 1); the same single dense-stand quadrat; annual net leaf production 154.9–243.5 g DW m⁻² yr⁻¹, P/Bmax 2.95–3.25 yr⁻¹
claims.note: It is a dense pure stand's leaf-blade peak, not a bed-average or whole-plant standing crop; the table row's label 'watershield leaves' is right. Grazing by the leaf beetle Galerucella nipponensis damaged 10–30 % of leaf area in early summer and < 10 % by August (p. 284).

notes: Both values the paper takes are in the paper as stated. Other values that may serve the model: annual net production of floating leaves 154.9–243.5 g DW m⁻² yr⁻¹; leaf turnover (vegetation period / mean life span) 6.0–6.3 per season; maximum LAI 0.90–1.36; new leaves appear at the surface from late May to late October with birth-rate peaks in May–June and August–September (Fig. 2); net production and leaf mass rose with cumulative sunshine duration from 1 May to late September (P < 0.05 and P < 0.005), not with cumulative temperature. The site is a Japanese irrigation pond (warm-temperate), so the season is longer than at Hot Brook.
